Do the backdoor Roth

Your income profile makes this close to a no-brainer, and your accounts are set up perfectly for it.

Why direct Roth is risky for you: Your base salary alone is $60,000/year (gross $2,500 semi-monthly), plus you had a single RSU vest of $42,000 in May and roughly $1,200/month in Figma consulting income. Why backdoor is clean for you specifically: Your Fidelity Traditional IRA balance is currently $0. That matters a lot — the backdoor Roth's only real risk is the "pro-rata rule," which taxes you proportionally if you already hold pre-tax IRA money. With a zero balance, you can contribute nondeductible dollars and convert to Roth immediately with essentially no tax cost.

Why not skip it: A nondeductible Traditional IRA contribution wouldn't even be deductible for you anyway — the 2026 deduction phase-out for someone covered by a workplace plan (your 401k) is $81,000–$91,000 MAGI, and you're above that. So there's no deduction being given up by going the Roth route instead of a plain Traditional IRA. That leaves the Roth version strictly better: same nondeductible contribution, but decades of tax-free growth instead of tax-deferred growth. With no existing balance to complicate the conversion, there's no real downside to doing it.

Convert it to your Roth IRA within a few days — leave it in cash/money market first so there's no gain to tax on conversion.
